description: Turn build123d CAD model functions into live, interactive parametric web UIs with the @app.part() decorator; typed signatures become sliders, checkboxes, and dropdowns.
rules: Every @app.part() parameter must have a default value; defaults define the initial build.
Use Annotated[float, Range(min, max, step, unit)] for sliders; bool for checkboxes; Literal or Enum for dropdowns; bare int/float for number inputs.
Range requires min < max; exclusive bounds (gt/lt) and one-sided ge/le raise ParamError at decoration time.
Write parts as compositions of small top-level functions in the same file; only same-file, top-level functions are cached.
Avoid Builder mode (with BuildPart():) inside cached functions; it bypasses the cache. Prefer algebra mode.
Impure names (open, random, time, environ, input, import_step, import_svg) in a function body disable caching for it and all its callers.
Functions reading module-level constants or sibling-module imports can serve stale cache entries; mark them @no_cache.
@no_cache is contagious: every caller of a no_cache function also runs uncached.
Label every child solid and return a flat Compound(children=[...]) so the mesh cache can hit.
fastbuild export validates --param values strictly against Range; out-of-range values error rather than clamp.
Run 'fastbuild agent-docs' for the full agent skill doc, or 'fastbuild view --debug' to trace cache HIT/MISS/BYPASS.
Requires Python 3.10-3.13; ~500 MB install; Alpine/musl unsupported.
